newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sony, Toyota group co mulling joint LCD venture.
newsitem.headline: Sony, Toyota group co mulling joint LCD venture.

text.p: Japan's two big brand names Sony Corp, and the Toyota Motor group are discussing a plan to jointly develop a electronics components business, expanding their already extensive reach into new fields.

Sony and Toyoda Automatic Loom Works Ltd, a group firm of Toyota Motor Corp, said on Wednesday that they are considering forming a joint venture to produce next-generation liquid crystal displays (LCD).
LCDs are at present used mainly as displays for notebook computers, but are expected to be widely used in desktop computers and TVs when the prices are lowered.
"The idea is we may be able to combine Sony's know-how in LCD and Toyoda's manufacturing technology," a Sony spokesman said.
"We are discussing a possibility for a joint business," a Toyoda spokesman said, adding the agreement could be made in a not too distant future.

Toyota, intent on searching new sources of income for the car giant group, recently made headlines with its plan, now shelved, to jump into profitable but risky computer memory chip production with Texas Instruments Inc.
"The chip production plan with TI has been shelved since the downfall of the chip market," the spokesman said.
Sony has developed a new type of LCDs, called polysilicon thin-film transistor (TFT) LCDs and is currently producing a small volume of the new type of LCDs for use in its video camcorders.
Sony said its technology allows production of large-size LCDs of about 20-inches, about twice the size of the panels now used in notebook PCs, in the future at low costs.
"The agreement, if it is reached, would mean Sony in full-fledged production of LCDs," the Sony spokesman said.
According to the financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun, Sony and Toyoda plan to form a joint venture by the end of this year.

The two companies will spend 50 billion to 60 billion yen ($517 million) to build a factory in Aichi Prefecture in Western Japan, which will start production as early as in the second half of the 1998/99 business year, the paper said.
The Toyota group decided to enter the LCD business as the device may be commonly used in cars in the future in displays for navigation systems, the paper said.
Analysts expect the market for polysilicon LCDs to grow sharply within few years.
Yoshiharu Izumi, analyst at UBS Securities, said he expects the market to balloon to around 300 billion yen ($2.58 billion) a year by 2000.
"It's (the agreement) is good to Sony as it can lessen the financial burden involved in the LCD production," he said.
Sony, aggressively diversifying its new businesses, has recently announced an entry into the costly digital satellite broadcasting business.
